findings.title: Generated outputs collide with initiative 320's audit-artifact exemption while claiming independence from 320
findings.description: The Dependencies section states 360 is "Independent of … 300, and 320 — no pipeline, judging, or agent-provider machinery is involved." Mechanically true, but the artifact shape couples them. `src/squadron/metrology/audit.py` defines `_AUDIT_ARTIFACT_PATTERN` as `project-documents/(?:user/(?:analysis/(?:\d+-analysis\..+\.md)?)?)?|…` — any *untracked* file matching `NNN-analysis.<anything>.md` under `user/analysis/` is exempted from `preflight_project(require_clean=True)` as "the audit's own output." Both proposed output shapes — `{index}-analysis.overview.md` and `{index}-analysis.codebase-comprehension.md` — match that pattern exactly. Likewise `find_audit_file` globs `project-documents/user/analysis/*-analysis.*.md` and returns the max-mtime match; without a time window a fresh 360 document can be returned as "the audit file." The effects are mostly benign today (a generated document is not a code change, so exemption is arguably the desired outcome), but the misattribution is unstated, untested in either initiative, and contradicts the independence claim. Slice design should either pick a naming segment 320's harness can attribute precisely, schedule the 320-side pattern tightening as an explicit coordination, or document why the conflation is acceptable.

findings.title: Output Conventions contradicts Capability 1's concept output
findings.description: The section opens: "Both capabilities write to the existing `project-documents/user/analysis/` directory with the existing `docType: analysis`." But Capability 1's Outputs place `000-concept.{project}.md` in `project-documents/user/project-guides/` with `docType: concept`, and the third output (initiative-plan candidates) has no stated location at all. The normative summary is wrong for one of three outputs and silent on another — a slice designer reading only Output Conventions would misplace the concept document.

findings.title: The 950+ index "sanction" is self-granted against a convention this repo does not own
findings.description: "Overflow into 950+ is sanctioned" — sanctioned by whom is unstated. `file-naming-conventions.md` lives in the `ai-project-guide` submodule (per `.gitmodules`), which is not checked out in this tree, so neither the claimed 940-949 reservation nor any overflow rule can be verified from here; the only in-repo corroboration is `commands/analysis/tech-debt-audit.md`'s "nnn starts at 940 (analysis range)," which states no upper bound. The mechanical gate (slice 172's `sq validate docs` / `cf validate frontmatter`) validates status, docType, dates, and required fields — not index bands — so 950+ files would pass the gate while violating the prose convention, exactly the "convention that is only written down is a suggestion" failure shape slice 172 was built to eliminate. The arch acknowledges the band "may need to be widened or re-cut later" yet commits to writing 950+ documents now. Either make the overflow contingent on the guide-repo change (the same cross-repo seam DEVLOG records for `revision_number:`) or cite the convention text that permits it.

findings.title: Capability 1's preconditions assume a cf-managed project it exists to serve
findings.description: The design goal — "Everything written lands in `project-documents/user/` with correct docType frontmatter and index conventions, so downstream phases and `cf` introspection consume it unchanged" — presupposes the conventions already exist in the target. But the motivating scenario is "a codebase that was never planned in squadron": a repo that may have no `project-documents/` tree, no CLAUDE.md convention pointers, and no frontmatter gate. Flow step 1 checks only plugin installation and graph presence; it never checks whether the target is cf-managed. The nearest prior art handled this explicitly: `metrology/audit.py` searches both `analysis/` and `project-documents/user/analysis/` because "both are real locations and both are searched — observed in practice." The arch must state what happens in a bare repo — bootstrap the tree (and which conventions get installed), write to bare `analysis/`, or refuse with instruction. Unspecified, this is where the first real run fails.

findings.title: The initiative-plan-candidates output has no path, docType, or naming, and looks deferrable
findings.description: Three outputs are listed; two have full paths, docType, and frontmatter treatment. Candidates have none. There is no representation for a "candidate" in the fifteen-value DocType enum (`src/squadron/documents/schema.py`); writing one as `docType: initiative-plan` would put a commitment document's type on a non-commitment artifact — which the arch itself calls "worse than none." Either specify the representation (e.g., candidates as a section inside the comprehension analysis document, requiring no new artifact or convention change) or cut candidates from this initiative and ship the two well-specified outputs; the concept and analysis documents carry the initiative's core value on their own.

findings.title: The overview's lifecycle is undefined: regeneration, staleness, and index semantics
findings.description: The index-range paragraph adopts the audit series' semantics — "each run is an independent sample rather than a revision of the last" — for both capabilities. That fits comprehension runs; it does not fit the overview, which is a derived, revisable artifact whose required input (the initiative plan, status `in_progress` in squadron's own repo) changes constantly. Unspecified: does a refresh burn a new index (littering `user/analysis/` with stale client-facing documents, each implicitly current — the exact "overstates progress" liability the Status rule warns about), overwrite in place, or use revision suffixes (`-1`, `-2`, per `000-process-journal.md` and the naming convention)? Nothing marks a stale overview or records which initiative-plan commit produced it, even though the whole document's value proposition is honesty.

findings.title: Repeat-run behavior for capability 1's own outputs is unspecified — including a sacred-section hazard
findings.description: The flow specifies graph-staleness handling but nothing about re-running the skill when its own outputs already exist. Does a second comprehension run overwrite `000-concept.{project}.md`? The project convention makes `## User-Provided Concept` sacred and "never rewritten" — a wholesale regeneration would destroy the first run's interview answers unless the skill diffs and preserves. The tech-debt-audit skill solved the identical problem with an explicit repeat-run / independent-run protocol; this arch has no counterpart. Note also the incoherence: the analysis output follows increment-per-run indexing, but the concept's path is fixed at index 000 — the two artifacts necessarily follow different revision models, and neither is stated.

findings.title: The concept output path `000-concept.{project}.md` conflicts with the only in-repo precedent
findings.description: The sole concept precedent in this ecosystem is the squadron initiative plan's own frontmatter: `source: user/project-guides/001-concept.squadron.md` — base index 001, shared with its initiative plan ("related documents share a base index"). The arch pins `000-concept.{project}.md` as the canonical output for every project. The concept guide that would settle the question lives in the `ai-project-guide` submodule (not checked out here), so this cannot be resolved from the repo — but an architecture that pins an exact filename for its primary artifact while the only observable precedent uses a different index should verify before slice design; generating `000-concept` into a project whose conventions expect `001-concept` breaks the lineage the frontmatter gate and `cf` introspection rely on.

findings.title: The external graph contract has no validation, degradation, or drift policy
findings.description: The contract table is asserted from the plugin's reference at v2.8.1 — the same document that describes upstream as "actively developed," i.e., a drift risk. Nothing specifies: (a) behavior when `tour[]` is empty or absent in an otherwise valid graph, despite the tour being "a strong signal for a concept's Solution Approach section" — the design's single most load-bearing input; (b) a required-keys shape validation at read time — per the project's own no-silent-fallback principle, a drifted v2.9 graph (renamed keys, changed node-type vocabulary) must fail explicitly, not yield a confidently wrong concept; (c) Flow step 1 conflates "plugin installed" with "graph exists" — a graph-absent repo yields the instruction "run `/understand`" even when the actual problem is the plugin isn't installed, a misleading remediation the Non-Goals section says the skill should "detect and instruct" on distinctly.

findings.title: "Must appear in the generated document's provenance" — the carrier is undefined and the obvious one is externally owned
findings.description: Neither Flow step 1 nor the Resolved Design Decisions defines what "the document's provenance" physically is. The natural carrier — a frontmatter key — sits on contested ground: `src/squadron/documents/schema.py`'s docstring says "Context Forge owns the frontmatter schema," and DEVLOG records this exact seam for `revision_number:` — "whether CF's own frontmatter consumers tolerate an unregistered key must be confirmed before it is proposed." Yet the existing audit files carry an unregistered `model:` key per the tech-debt-audit skill, so the evidence on tolerance is contradictory. The arch neither schedules that confirmation nor picks an alternative (e.g., a mandated body-level provenance section). Resolve the carrier before slice design; staleness provenance is the mechanism the arch itself calls the guard against "a confidently wrong concept doc."

findings.title: The read-discipline strategy presumes a greppable graph serialization
findings.description: "Grep for the needed section before reading; never load the whole file into context" only works if `knowledge-graph.json` is pretty-printed. Compact single-line JSON — the shape this repo's own sample extraction uses (`reference/repowire-probe-sample.json` is one line) — makes grep return the entire file as one "line," defeating the discipline. Verify the plugin's actual serialization before relying on it; otherwise the skill needs field-targeted extraction (e.g., `jq`) rather than grep.

findings.title: "Features become outcomes" and "derive, never invent" pull against each other, and the document's own example straddles the line
findings.description: The example translates "weighted review convergence with decay-based finding dismissal" (initiative 180, status `not_started`) into "automated review that converges without human babysitting" — an outcome claim no input artifact asserts. Benefits are "derived from initiative descriptions," including not_started ones, so the document will carry benefit claims about unbuilt work with only the Status field hedging. Slice design should pin the boundary: benefits of planned work are phrased as planned outcomes, or they move to the Roadmap field.

findings.title: Load-bearing current-state and delivery claims verify against the repo
findings.description: Verified directly: `commands/sq/analysis.md` routes only `tech-debt-audit` and contains exactly the three edit sites the Delivery section enumerates (valid-skills line, usage block, skill section); `commands/analysis/` contains only `tech-debt-audit.md`, forked from `ksimback/tech-debt-skill` per its header comment; `.gitignore` has no `understand`/`trash` entries; `commands/sq/summary.md` exists (the premise for rejecting `summary` as the capability-(b) name); `reference/analyze-codebase-prompt.md` exists and matches its "retained, not superseded" description; `DocumentStatus` in `src/squadron/documents/schema.py` is exactly the five values the Status-values paragraph lists, with `draft` absent; analysis docs 940/941/942 exist as claimed. The external-contract claims (tour provenance, plugin paths, upstream issue #301) remain unverified against the plugin itself and are covered by the contract findings above.
